notes: The page is an ink manuscript continuation, without a separate ink page number at its head. Pale pencil 70 is kept as margin foliation with uncertain hand attribution. The slanted epsilon_1 note, the parenthesized annotation near (85), all four cancellations and all four inserted items are transcribed. The curve beside raised I is its connector, not an extra opening parenthesis. The smaller annotation near (85) is linked to the bottom-left brace by a curve; its text remains a margin note rather than H’s underbrace.

The manuscript associates a four-element set I amalg tilde A prime_0, furnished with a partition of type (2,2), with its set J of three partitions of that type. A marked epsilon_1 is distinguished; the other two points form J prime=I wedge_(Z/2) tilde A prime_0. A limited independent arithmetic check enumerated the unordered pair partitions of {1,2,3,4}: precisely 12|34, 13|24 and 14|23. That checks only the elementary count three; it neither proves the graph/torsor identifications nor determines a doubtful handwritten digit.

The manuscript describes the projective line indexed by J as a compactification of G_m^1 wedge_(±1) J prime with an S_(J prime), isomorphic to Z/2, action by transfer of structure. It gives the two identifications in (85) and states that S_I acts through S_(J prime), hence trivially on M-hat_(D_0). These geometric/action assertions are carried as manuscript claims, not proved in this reading.

The manuscript names the J prime trajectory P_0 and the epsilon_1 trajectory P_1 as two points at infinity. Formula (86) writes M_(D_0) isomorphic to E_Z^1 minus section 2 and equal to Spec Z[T]_(T−2), preserving that localization notation. It displays M_(G_0)→M_(D_0), T→T+1/T. Formula (87) describes M-hat_(D_0) using P_Z^1 with “signature” 2 along T=2. No proof of these moduli identifications or interpretation of the localization convention is claimed.

For f(x)=x+1/x, direct exact arithmetic gives f(1)=2 and f(−1)=−2. Its derivative 1−1/x² vanishes at x=±1; the second derivative 2/x³ takes nonzero values 2 and −2 there. Thus both ±2 are branch values of this rational map over characteristic zero. The sole section specified in (87), T=2, does not record the other branch value. This calculation neither proves a stack description nor addresses characteristic 2. It flags a question for mathematical review and does not authorize changing the written T=2 to −2.

Local source forms are preserved: associe has no detached final accent; the compactifying glyph has lower m; all three raised A strokes are primes, while Gamma in (85) has an upright and distinct dot for !; (86) has a doubled E rather than A. All five ordinary live D indices use the local small oval 0, without a pointed-loop graphic. The first On a ends in one detached point, transcribed as a period. Both arrows in the via display are plain arrows. The section T in (87) is overworked, but its large top bar survives and there is no minus before 2.

Thirty physical rows were read: twenty-four main-body rows, including one row for the first display, two for (85), one for (86), two for the via map and two for (87); two slanted marginal rows; one parenthesized annotation row; one extra band for the raised I/J/3 insertions; one extra row for inserted P_0; and one pencil-foliation row. Canceled material on shared baselines was not counted again. The whole scan and both native halves were read before eighteen saved crops; every crop was viewed. No OCR, internet research, TeX compilation, other page, or blind second reading was used.

H’s editorial note about its doubtful compactifying symbol and its note claiming continuation of (87) are not manuscript ink. Its separate (?) reading flag is treated as editorial, not as a handwritten question. This page has two physical rows for (87) and a closing parenthesis at the bottom edge.
